madretsch.title: Madretsch Mosque
madretsch.excerptHome: Construction and fitting out of the Madretsch Mosque, the first major project of Fondation Wakef.
madretsch.excerpt: The first major project of Fondation Wakef: construction and fitting out of the Madretsch Mosque in Biel/Bienne. A space of 496 m² serving the Muslim community of Madretsch.
madretsch.subtitle: The first major project of Fondation Wakef Suisse
madretsch.intro: The Madretsch Mosque, opened in 2009 in Biel/Bienne, is the first major project of Fondation Wakef Suisse. With its 496 m², it welcomes the Muslim community of the Madretsch district and forms the ground on which the Foundation built its expertise in Islamic funding in Switzerland.
objectifs: Create a dignified place of worship for the Muslim community of Madretsch
Provide a setting for learning the Arabic language and for Islamic education
Foster integration and shared community life within the local fabric of Biel/Bienne
madretsch.description: As the first major project of the Foundation, the Madretsch Mosque shows the ability of Fondation Wakef to carry Islamic infrastructure projects in Switzerland through to completion. It laid the foundations of our operating model: transparent community funding, professional management and strong local roots.
madretsch.avancement: Project completed and fully in use since 2009. The mosque welcomes the Madretsch community every day and is a steady landmark for the whole region.
madretsch.vision: The Madretsch Mosque remains a reference model: a place of worship well settled in its district, serving a diverse and united community, a symbol of the permanence that Fondation Wakef seeks to embody.

aliman.title: Al Iman Centre
aliman.excerptHome: An Islamic centre open to all nationalities: a spirit of complete openness in the heart of Fribourg.
aliman.excerpt: An Islamic centre run by the Albanian Cultural Association (CCA), with a spirit of complete openness that rises above nationalities to welcome the whole Fribourg community.
aliman.subtitle: An Islamic centre open to all nationalities
aliman.intro: The Al Iman Centre in Fribourg, run by the Albanian Cultural Association (CCA), embodies a spirit of complete openness: rising above nationalities to welcome the whole Muslim community of Fribourg. Built in 1997, it covers 132 m² in the heart of the city.
objectifs: Renovate and modernise the premises to welcome worshippers better
Offer a place of worship that reaches beyond national and cultural boundaries
Strengthen the bond between the Muslim community and Fribourg society
aliman.description: The Al Iman Centre stands out for its spirit of complete openness: its doors are open to all nationalities and cultures, beyond the origins of the association that runs it. It is a place of meeting, learning and prayer for the whole Muslim community of Fribourg, reflecting the cosmopolitan character of the city.
aliman.avancement: Renovation works partly completed. Fondation Wakef is supporting the CCA association in finishing the interior fittings and making the best use of the spaces.
aliman.vision: To make the Al Iman Centre a model of integration and openness, where the diversity of Swiss Islam finds its most harmonious expression: a community centre in the fullest sense of the word.

albadr.title: Al Badr Centre
albadr.excerptHome: The only mosque on the border between Switzerland and France: renovation of a historic building from 1902.
albadr.excerpt: The only mosque on the border between Switzerland and France: renovation of a historic building from 1902 and an extension of 1,400 m² for a large Islamic cultural centre.
albadr.subtitle: The only mosque on the border between Switzerland and France
albadr.intro: The Al Badr Centre in Le Locle is a project of singular scale: on a plot of 2,029 m², of which 600 m² are already built and 1,400 m² are set aside for the extension, it is the only mosque on the border between Switzerland and France. The existing building, put up in 1902, is of remarkable architectural interest.
objectifs: Complete renovation of the historic building from 1902
Modern construction of an extension of 1,400 m²
Create the only Islamic cultural hub on the border between Switzerland and France
albadr.description: The Al Badr Centre is the most ambitious project of Fondation Wakef. A few steps from the French border, it serves a community unlike any other, living on both sides of that border. The project combines the preservation of a remarkable architectural heritage (the building of 1902) with a resolutely modern vision for its extension.
albadr.avancement: Phase 1 completed: the men's prayer hall (70 m²) and the women's prayer hall (60 m²) are in use. Phase 2 under way: complete renovation of the historic building and construction of the extension of 1,400 m².
albadr.vision: To make the Al Badr Centre a leading Islamic cultural centre for the communities of Le Locle and the neighbouring French regions, bringing heritage and modernity together in a place that is unique in Switzerland.

annour.title: An-Nour Mosque
annour.excerpt: The first Arabic speaking mosque in the canton of Valais. Phase 1 (210 m²) completed; Phase 2 (210 m²) under way, with a promise of sale valid until the end of 2026.
annour.subtitle: The first Arabic speaking mosque in Valais
annour.intro: The An-Nour Mosque in Sion is a landmark project: as the first Arabic speaking mosque in the canton of Valais, it meets the needs of a community that until now had no suitable place of worship. With a budget of CHF 900,000 and an area of 420 m², the project is being carried out in two phases by the An-Nour Association.
objectifs: Give Valais its first Arabic speaking mosque, dignified and fit for purpose
Complete both construction phases (210 m² + 210 m²)
Root the Arabic speaking community lastingly in the Sion region

fiche.label: Phase 2
fiche.value: 210 m², promise of sale until the end of 2026

annour.description: Valais is home to a large Arabic speaking Muslim community that long went without a place of worship to match. The An-Nour Mosque, led by the An-Nour Association with the support of Fondation Wakef, fills this historic gap. Phase 1, covering 210 m², is already in use.
annour.avancement: Phase 1 (210 m²): completed and in use. Phase 2 (210 m²): promise of sale signed, valid until the end of 2026. Fundraising is under way to complete the purchase and the works.
annour.vision: To make the An-Nour Mosque the spiritual heart of the Arabic speaking community of Valais: a place of prayer, learning and community life for present and future generations.

bibliotheque.title: Mobile Library
bibliotheque.excerpt: “Ponts du Savoir” (Bridges of Knowledge): a multilingual travelling library that fosters intercultural dialogue. Slogan: “Let us get to know one another. Knowledge brings us together.”
bibliotheque.subtitle: “Ponts du Savoir” (Bridges of Knowledge): knowledge brings us together
bibliotheque.intro: The Mobile Library “Ponts du Savoir” (Bridges of Knowledge) is a project unlike any other in Romandy (French speaking Switzerland): a multilingual travelling library devoted to intercultural dialogue. It moves between cultural events, public spaces and everyday meeting places to reach communities where they are.
objectifs: Foster intercultural dialogue through the sharing of knowledge
Make multilingual resources available to every community
Train ambassadors of intercultural dialogue in Romandy
bibliotheque.description: Under the slogan “Let us get to know one another. Knowledge brings us together.”, the Mobile Library travels across Romandy to build bridges between communities. The team of ambassadors carries not only books, but also stories, languages and the impulse of a genuine encounter between people of different cultures.
bibliotheque.avancement: The programme has been running since 2023. It is regularly present at cultural events and in public spaces across Romandy. The network of ambassadors keeps growing.
bibliotheque.vision: To make the Mobile Library “Ponts du Savoir” a national reference for intercultural dialogue through education, drawing on the universal power of knowledge to bring people together.

delal-el-khayr.title: Shades of Charity, Le Locle
delal-el-khayr.excerptHome: Acquisition of an investment property to transform into a multifunctional Islamic Centre in Le Locle
delal-el-khayr.excerpt: We are raising funds to acquire and renovate an investment property in Le Locle, which will become a comprehensive Islamic centre offering: mosque, training halls, residential units, and commercial space.
delal-el-khayr.subtitle: Multifunctional Islamic Centre
delal-el-khayr.surfaceDetail: 5 storeys · 6 apartments · 1 commercial unit · 5 parking spaces · 2 buildable plots
delal-el-khayr.intro: Wakef Switzerland Foundation is working to acquire an investment property in Le Locle, transforming an existing building into a comprehensive Islamic Centre: mosque, teaching halls, residential spaces, commercial unit, and developable land.
objectifs: Building acquisition: CHF 1'250'000 (CHF 550'000 to raise)
Renovation and adaptation for multiple uses
Creation of a mosque and prayer space
Training and educational halls
Residential spaces for caretaker and volunteers
Commercial unit generating income: CHF 49'380 annual net revenue
Two buildable plots for future expansion
delal-el-khayr.description: Le Locle needs a fully functional Islamic centre. This acquisition offers a unique solution: an investment property that partially finances its own development through rental income.
delal-el-khayr.vision: A welcoming Islamic centre: mosque, education, residential units, commerce, generating stable revenue for the Foundation and serving the Le Locle community.

about.p1: The Fondation Wakef Suisse was established in 2009 under article 80 of the Swiss Civil Code and is registered under the number CHE-114.901.246. It was born of a deep conviction: the Muslim community of Switzerland deserves institutions that are enduring, independent and rigorously governed.
about.p2After: refers to the Islamic concept of a perpetual endowment: an asset or a sum irrevocably devoted to a cause of public benefit, whose income serves the community generation after generation.
about.missionText: To promote positive citizenship through a balanced educational and religious framework. Our work covers the upkeep of places of worship, the training of imams, support for scientific research and academic guidance for young people.
about.visionText: To establish institutional governance that secures the financial independence of Muslim institutions in Switzerland, so that their contribution endures for future generations.

hero.label: Pillar of Islam
hero.title: Zakat Calculator
hero.sub: Work out your annual Zakat obligation according to the rules of Sharia. Current Nisab: CHF/€ 4,600 (≈ 85g of gold).

zakat.toolBody: Enter the value of your assets in Swiss francs or in euros. Zakat is due if your net wealth has exceeded the Nisab for a full lunar year (Hawl).
zakat.belowNisab: ℹ️ Your net wealth is below the Nisab (CHF {{nisab}}). You do not owe Zakat al-Māl this year.
zakat.nisabInfo: ℹ️ The Nisab is set at the value of 85g of gold (~CHF 4,600). Zakat is due if your net wealth has exceeded this threshold for a full lunar year (Hawl).
zakat.estimateNote: This calculation is an indicative estimate.

explain.title: The Nisab النصاب
explain.desc: The Nisab is the minimum threshold of wealth. It is set at the value of 85g of gold (or 595g of silver, depending on the school of law). In 2025 this corresponds to about CHF 4,600. The amount is revised in line with the price of gold.

explain.title: The Hawl الحول
explain.desc: The Hawl is the condition of duration: your wealth must remain above the Nisab for a full lunar year (about 354 days) for Zakat to become obligatory.

explain.title: The rate of 2.5%
explain.desc: The rate of Zakat on monetary wealth (Zakat al-Māl) is 2.5% of taxable net wealth, that is the total of your assets less your short term debts.

explain.title: What is subject to Zakat
explain.desc: Subject to Zakat: physical gold and silver, cash, bank accounts, shares (market value), savings and halal investments. Not subject to Zakat: your main residence, your personal vehicle and goods for personal use.

faq.q: Can I pay my Zakat in several instalments?
faq.a: Yes, Zakat may be paid in several instalments over the course of the lunar year, as long as the full amount is settled before the anniversary date (Hawl). It is nevertheless better to pay it in one go, so that no deadline is forgotten.

faq.q: How do I calculate Zakat on a salary?
faq.a: For employees, Zakat is calculated on the net savings built up over the year, not on the gross salary. Work out the savings you still hold (income less necessary spending) at the end of a lunar year. If those savings exceed the Nisab, you owe 2.5% on them.

faq.q: My calculator says “Below the Nisab”: am I exempt?
faq.a: If your net wealth is below the Nisab (~CHF 4,600), you do not owe Zakat al-Māl. You may still give a voluntary Sadaqah at any time.

For entrepreneurs, property held for resale, cryptocurrencies or complex financial situations, we recommend consulting a qualified Islamic scholar or our Sharia Committee. Write to us at info@wakf.ch.

zakat.noteBody: Our calculator covers standard cases. For entrepreneurs, owners of commercial property, investors or unusual financial situations, our Sharia Committee can guide you.

hero.label: Fondation Wakef Suisse
hero.title: Frequently asked questions
hero.sub: All the answers about the Foundation, donations, Zakat and our projects. A question still unanswered? Write to us.

items.q: What is the Fondation Wakef Suisse?
items.a: The Fondation Wakef Suisse is a foundation under Swiss private law (Art. 80 CC), registered under CHE-114.901.246 and founded in 2009. It funds Islamic infrastructure projects in Switzerland: mosques, Islamic centres, scholarships and Muslim burial sections in cemeteries.

The Foundation is supervised by the Federal Supervisory Authority for Foundations. It has independent auditors who examine the accounts every year, and a Sharia Committee that confirms the Islamic compliance of every project.

items.q: How large is the endowment capital?
items.a: The initial endowment capital is CHF 50,000, in accordance with the statutes registered in 2009. All the funds collected are added to this capital and are used exclusively for the projects of the Foundation.

items.q: How do I make a donation?
items.a: You can donate through our online form on the “Donate” page, by bank transfer (details available on request at info@wakf.ch), or by post to our contact office in Biel/Bienne.

items.q: Can I make a recurring (monthly) donation?
items.a: Yes. You can choose a monthly donation by saying so on the form. Our team will then contact you to set up the standing order.

items.q: Is the Foundation transparent in the way it is run?
items.a: Yes. The Fondation Wakef Suisse is subject to Swiss civil law (Art. 80 CC) and supervised by the cantonal supervisory authority for foundations of the canton of Vaud. The accounts are examined every year by independent auditors and the financial reports are available on request at info@wakf.ch.

items.q: Can I make a donation dedicated to a specific project?
items.a: Yes. When you donate, you can name the project you wish to support among our five projects: Madretsch Mosque (Biel/Bienne), Al Iman Centre (Fribourg), Al Badr Centre (Le Locle), An-Nour Mosque (Sion) and the Mobile Library “Ponts du Savoir”. If that project is fully funded, the money will go to the priority project under way.

items.q: How do I calculate my Zakat?
items.a: Use our Zakat calculator on the /zakat page. Enter your assets (gold, silver, liquid assets, investments) and your short term debts. If your net wealth has exceeded the Nisab (CHF/€ 4,600) for a lunar year, you owe 2.5% of that amount.
The Nisab is the minimum threshold of wealth. It is set at the value of 85g of gold, about CHF 4,600 in 2025. If your net wealth is below this threshold, you do not owe Zakat al-Māl.
Yes. Zakat al-Fitr is an obligatory act of charity paid at the end of Ramadan, whatever your wealth. Its amount is set each year by Islamic scholars (usually between CHF 10 and 20 per person).

Fondation Wakef funds five projects: Madretsch Mosque in Biel/Bienne (completed, 496 m²), Al Iman Centre in Fribourg (ongoing, 132 m²), Al Badr Centre in Le Locle (ongoing, 2,029 m²), An-Nour Mosque in Sion (ongoing, 420 m²) and the Mobile Library “Ponts du Savoir” in Romandy. See the Projects page for full details.

Each donation goes to a general fund or to a specific project, according to your choice. The Foundation Board approves the allocation of the funds, and an annual report sets out the use of every franc collected.

items.q: Can I dedicate my donation to a specific project?
items.a: Yes. When you donate, you can name the project you wish to support (Madretsch Mosque, Al Iman Centre or Al Badr Centre). If that project is already funded, the money will go to the most urgent project.

hero.label: Official documents
hero.title: Statutes of the Foundation
hero.sub: The official statutes of the Fondation Wakef Suisse, registered under CHE-114.901.246 pursuant to Art. 80 CC. Adopted on 5 June 2009, amended on 13 April 2018.

statutes.cardLine2: Founded on 5 June 2009 · Amended on 13 April 2018
statutes.cardLine3: Art. 80 ss Swiss Civil Code · Registered office: Prilly (VD)

articles.contenu: Under the name “Fondation WAKEF SUISSE” (hereinafter “the Foundation”), a foundation under Swiss private law is established within the meaning of articles 80 and following of the Swiss Civil Code. The duration of the Foundation is unlimited.
The registered office of the Foundation is in Prilly, in the canton of Vaud (Switzerland).

The purpose of the Foundation is to support and fund projects of a religious, educational, social and humanitarian nature, in keeping with the values of Islam and in compliance with Swiss law. The Foundation carries out its activities exclusively in Switzerland. It pursues in particular the following objectives: (1) to build, buy and renovate Muslim places of worship; (2) to contribute to the training of imams and to their integration into Swiss society; (3) to support schools of Arabic language and Muslim culture; (4) to award scholarships to Muslim students; (5) to encourage charitable, educational, scientific and sociocultural activities; (6) to support the creation of Muslim burial sections in Swiss cemeteries.

The endowment capital is set at CHF 50,000 (fifty thousand Swiss francs) in cash. The Foundation manages this capital according to the principles of liquidity, security, return and risk spreading. This capital is inalienable and is devoted exclusively to the purposes of the Foundation.

The resources of the Foundation come from the endowment capital and its income, from gifts and legacies of natural or legal persons, from grants awarded by public or private bodies, and from any other income compatible with the purpose of the Foundation.

The members of the governing bodies of the Foundation are liable for the damage they cause intentionally or through negligence in the exercise of their functions, in accordance with the provisions of the Swiss Code of Obligations.
The governing bodies of the Foundation are: the Foundation Board (FB), the Executive Committee (EC), also called the Bureau, the Working Group (WG), and the Auditors.

The Foundation Board is made up of 7 to 10 members, all of the Muslim faith. At least three quarters of the members must be resident in Switzerland. Members are appointed by cooptation with a two thirds majority of the serving members. Members carry out their duties on a voluntary basis.

The Foundation Board is the supreme body of the Foundation. It is competent to: define the strategic direction of the Foundation, grant signing authority on behalf of the Foundation, appoint and remove the members of the Executive Committee, approve the annual budget and the accounts, issue the internal regulations, and take any other decision reserved to the FB by these statutes.

The Foundation Board meets at least once a year. The agenda is sent to the members at least 30 days before the meeting. The quorum is reached when the majority of the members is present, necessarily including the President or the Vice President. Decisions are taken by a simple majority of the members present.

The Executive Committee (the Bureau) is made up of the President, the Vice President and the Secretary. The members of the Executive Committee are elected by the Foundation Board for a term of five years, which may be renewed.

The Executive Committee carries out the decisions of the Foundation Board and represents the Foundation towards third parties by the joint signature of two of its members. It draws up the annual budget and the balance sheet of the Foundation, and manages current business.
The Executive Committee meets at least four times a year to deal with current business and to follow the progress of the projects under way.

Any member of the Foundation Board may object to a decision of the Executive Committee within 30 days. The objection has suspensive effect and the contested decision is submitted to the Foundation Board.

The Auditors are external to and independent of the Foundation. They are appointed by the Foundation Board for a term of one year, which may be renewed. They examine the annual accounts and draw up a report for the Foundation Board and for the supervisory authority.
The financial year runs from 1 January to 31 December. The annual financial statements are submitted for approval to the Foundation Board within six months of the close of the financial year.
These statutes may be amended by a decision of the Foundation Board taken with a two thirds majority of the serving members. The purpose of the Foundation is inviolable and may not be amended.
The dissolution of the Foundation is governed by articles 88 and 89 of the Swiss Civil Code. It is ordered by the competent supervisory authority.

In the event of dissolution, the assets of the Foundation are transferred to one or more Swiss institutions under public law, or recognised as serving the public benefit, that pursue a similar purpose and are exempt from tax. This clause is inviolable. The founders irrevocably waive any right over the assets of the Foundation.

The Foundation is subject to the supervision of the competent authority in accordance with article 84 of the Swiss Civil Code and article 96 of the Commercial Register Ordinance (CRO). The Foundation may request an exemption from supervision in accordance with article 87 CC.
The Foundation is entered in the Commercial Register of the canton of Vaud.

sections.title: 1. Data controller
sections.content: The Fondation Wakef Suisse (CHE-114.901.246), Avenue de la Confrérie 11, 1008 Prilly (VD), is the controller of your personal data within the meaning of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and of the Federal Act on Data Protection (FADP).

sections.title: 2. Data collected
sections.content: We collect only the data we need: surname and first name, email address, telephone number (if provided), amount and type of donation, and any information you send us through the contact form.

sections.title: 3. Purposes of the processing
sections.content: Your data is used to: process your donation and issue a tax receipt, answer your enquiries, send our newsletter (with your consent), and meet our legal obligations (tax and accounting).

sections.title: 4. Legal bases
sections.content: The processing is based on: your consent (newsletter), the performance of a contract (donations), our legal obligations (tax receipts, accounting), and our legitimate interest (security and improvement of the service).

sections.title: 5. Retention period
sections.content: Your donation data is kept for 10 years (a Swiss legal obligation). Contact data is deleted on request or after 3 years without activity. Newsletter data is deleted as soon as you unsubscribe.

sections.title: 6. Sharing of the data
sections.content: Your data is never sold. It may be shared with: Formspree (processing of the forms), Mailchimp (newsletter), and the Swiss tax authorities (for tax receipts only).

sections.title: 7. Your rights
sections.content: Under the GDPR and the FADP, you have the right of access, rectification, erasure, portability and objection. To exercise these rights, write to us at info@wakf.ch.

sections.title: 8. Cookies
sections.content: Our site uses only the technical cookies needed for it to work (no advertising cookies and no third party tracking). You can disable cookies in your browser.

sections.title: 9. Contact and complaints
sections.content: For any question, please write to: info@wakf.ch · +41 79 379 96 46. You may also lodge a complaint with the Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC).
